narration: Welcome to the Central Asian Antiquities gallery, where we are delighted to present the Painted Silk Banner Fragment, accession number NM 08.221/19. This delicate piece, measuring 35 by 90 centimetres, dates to the Tang era of the 7th‑to‑9th century CE and was originally found in the Dandan‑Oilik oasis of Xinjiang along the ancient Silk Route. The silk bears fine brushwork and mineral pigments that depict a fragment of a Buddhist deity, a testament to the sophisticated textile traditions of the time. Its survival owes much to the dry desert climate of the Tarim Basin, and it was brought to us by Sir Aurel Stein during his Central Asian expeditions. As you explore, imagine this banner once fluttering in a shrine, a silent witness to the vibrant cultural exchanges that flowed along the Silk Road.
